test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 27 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: During COP30 held in November 2025, the term Conference of the Parties (COP) refers to the meeting of the Parties under which United Nations convention?

options.text: United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity (UNCBD)
Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES)
United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)

solution:
The correct answer is __**United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Conference of the Parties (COP)** serves as the supreme decision-making body of the **United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)**. It is responsible for reviewing the implementation of the Convention and any other legal instruments adopted by the body.
 
• **COP30** is scheduled to be held in **November 2025**. The host city for this milestone event is **Belém**, **Brazil**, marking a significant return of the climate summit to the **Amazon** region.
 
• The primary mandate of the **UNFCCC** is to achieve the stabilization of **greenhouse gas** concentrations in the atmosphere at a level that would prevent dangerous anthropogenic interference with the climate system.
 
• During these annual meetings, representatives from **198 Parties** (197 countries plus the European Union) gather to negotiate climate actions, assess progress, and refine strategies such as the **Paris Agreement**.
 
• The designation **COP30** specifically refers to the **30th** session of the Conference of the Parties to the **UNFCCC**. While other conventions like **UNCBD** also use the term COP, their numbering and meeting cycles differ. ***Hence, the correct answer is United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **UNFCCC Origins:** The convention was adopted on **May 9, 1992**, and was opened for signature at the **Earth Summit** in **Rio de Janeiro**, **Brazil**. It officially entered into force on **March 21, 1994**.
 
• **Major Agreements:** The **UNFCCC** provides the framework for two major international treaties: the **Kyoto Protocol (1997)** and the **Paris Agreement (2015)**. The **Paris Agreement** aims to limit the global temperature increase to well below **2 degrees Celsius** above pre-industrial levels.
 
• **UNCBD (United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity):** This is a separate "Rio Convention" focused on the conservation of biological diversity and the sustainable use of its components. Its COPs usually occur **biennially** (every two years).
 
• **CITES:** The **Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora** is an international agreement between governments to ensure that international trade in specimens of wild animals and plants does not threaten the survival of the species.
 
• **UNCAC:** The **United Nations Convention Against Corruption** is the only legally binding universal anti-corruption instrument, managed by the **UNODC**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of COP30:** **COP30** in **2025** is considered a critical juncture because parties are expected to submit their updated **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)**, which are the climate action plans to cut emissions and adapt to climate impacts.
 
• **Historical Context:** The first-ever COP (**COP1**) was held in **Berlin**, **Germany**, in **1995**. Since then, the meeting has rotated annually among the **five recognized UN regions**: Africa, Asia-Pacific, Eastern Europe, Latin America and the Caribbean, and Western Europe and Others.
 
• **The Secretariat:** The **UN Climate Change Secretariat** is the United Nations entity tasked with supporting the global response to the threat of climate change. It is located in **Bonn**, **Germany**.
 
• **Financial Mechanisms:** To support developing countries, the **UNFCCC** operates financial mechanisms including the **Global Environment Facility (GEF)** and the **Green Climate Fund (GCF)**.
